critical_code_review_comments: ProtectedImage.jsx: The watermark layer is conditionally rendered on `loaded && watermark`, where `loaded` is toggled by . If the errors out (e.g. broken URL, naturalWidth=0) the onLoad event never fires, so no .watermark-layer is rendered. In this run we briefly saw a stale TEST_photo with a broken /api/files/nophotopix/uploads/... URL on the home page that had hasWm=false. After deleting the orphan record the page was clean (8/8 watermarked). Suggestion (non-blocking): also set `loaded=true` on onError so the watermark always covers the alt-text fallback. Also consider using a useEffect that checks img.complete + naturalWidth > 0 on mount to handle cache-hit cases where onLoad fires before the React listener is attached — although this iteration's repeated reloads did not actually exhibit the cache-hit problem.
server.py L43: DOWNLOAD_TOKEN_TTL_HOURS = 48 and validate_order uses timedelta(hours=DOWNLOAD_TOKEN_TTL_HOURS) at L726. Confirmed runtime delta = 47h59m59s in test_validate_sets_48h_ttl.
Download.jsx grid correctly passes watermark={false} to ProtectedImage so paid users see clean HD previews. /success uses the default watermark=true on previews. Good separation.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Watermark gating: ProtectedImage only renders .watermark-layer when img.onLoad has fired (loaded=true). If you see a tile without watermark, first check img.naturalWidth — broken images won't get a watermark. To test watermark presence, prefer Unsplash seeded photos (their URLs always load). The /download/{token} grid intentionally has NO watermark (watermark={false}); do not assert otherwise. 48h TTL: validate_order uses DOWNLOAD_TOKEN_TTL_HOURS=48 (server.py L43). When SendGrid key invalid, /api/admin/orders/{id}/validate returns 502 with detail 'Commande validée mais email NON envoyé' but the order IS completed and download_token + download_expires_at are written — always re-GET /api/orders/{id} to read the final state. Test selectors used: [data-testid^='photo-tile-'], .protected-img > .watermark-layer (sibling of img), success-download-cta, download-photos-grid, download-photo-{id}.
rca of the issue: No new functional bugs introduced by this iteration's changes. The only frontend hiccup observed (one tile missing its watermark layer on the home page) was caused by stale DB data — a previously orphaned uploaded photo whose URL 404s — not by the new watermark code. Root cause of that single observation: ProtectedImage relies on img.onLoad to toggle the `loaded` state that gates rendering of .watermark-layer; for a 404 image, onLoad never fires, so the layer never appears. This is acceptable visually because the broken image area is empty anyway. Suggested non-blocking improvement: also set loaded=true on onError so the watermark covers the alt-text fallback (no action item created since it's outside the iteration scope).
